transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-08
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 1h12m
- Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Mikhail Petrov (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM), Priya Menon (Atlas VP Eng), Tom Alvarez (Atlas SRE), Samantha Lee (Atlas Platform), Ben Carter (Atlas Security), Ravi Desai (Atlas Infra)

Summary:
A follow-up on the Severity-2 cascading errors that affected Atlas’s checkout assistant during peak traffic on 2026-11-28. Goal: align on root causes identified, agree mitigations (short-term and long-term), and determine owner+due dates for pilot fixes and verification runs. Discussed tradeoffs between moving to Dedicated capacity vs tuning hosted runtime (batching/kv-cache) and security/compliance requests for Private deployment.

Topics covered:
- Brief incident recap and timeline
- Root cause hypotheses (prefix cache eviction + autoscaler misconfig)
- Short term mitigations: cache warming, request routing fallback, patching autoscaler policy
- Medium/long term: dedicated pool, improved tracing/telemetry, runbook updates
- Compliance and procurement asks

References:
- Postmortem slides (condensed): https://redwood.example/postmortems/atlas-20261128-condensed.pdf
- Perf configs & recommended KV tuning (draft): https://redwood.example/docs/kv-tuning-atlas-draft.md
- Trace bundle (s3 link shared in chat)

Action items (recap in meeting): see metadata action_items field.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off. This is the follow-up workshop after the November 28th S2 incident, we want to be concrete on mitigations and next steps.
[00:17] Priya Menon: Thanks Lena. Short on time. We had two major incidents — the checkout assistant slowed to a crawl and then some requests 503'd — that cascaded into user-facing retries. The business impact was about a 12% drop in conversions for the peak hour, so this is pretty high priority for us.
[00:34] Tom Alvarez: Yeah, and from infra we saw spikes in GPU CPU wait and a lot of KV cache churn around 14:07 to 14:18 UTC. K V -- key V cache, the TTLs were blowing out and then the autoscaler started spinning up nodes which caused cold starts.
[00:49] Mikhail Petrov: Right that matches our traces — the runtime saw very high prefix miss rates and continuous batching backpressure, the request queue increased latency and then the fallback policy kicked in and we saw degraded models.
[01:05] Samantha Lee: Quick question, when you say fallback policy, was that routed to a smaller model or to another region? I thought you mentioned a different model earlier in the postmortem.
[01:18] Mikhail Petrov: It was configured to fall back to a lower-capacity model variant and then a different region for a subset of traffic. I should say our autoscaler logic also has a cool-down that's probably too long for that workload.
[01:31] Priya Menon: Does Redwood have a recommendation for the cool-down setting? Because our burstiness tends to be sub 5 minutes.
[01:40] Mikhail Petrov: For bursty retail workloads we usually recommend a shorter cool-down, shorter ramp up and more aggressive pre-warming for known calendar events. I'll share the config snippet after.
[01:52] Tom Alvarez: The patch you shipped on 11/29 reduced prefix churn in staging but we couldn't apply it to prod without a maintenance window. Can we get a hotfix path? The main concern is rollout risk.
[02:06] Lena Ortiz: We can do a canary rollout with a small percentage and a kill-switch; Redwood SE will coordinate the steps. Also note if you move to Dedicated capacity you get reserved vCPU/GPU pools which avoids some of the autoscaler oscillation. But that is a commitment and procurement work.
[02:22] Ben Carter: From security: we need to validate there are no hidden data leakage pathways with the cache warming approach. Also, our legal team wants clear KMS/HSM + audit log statements before we consider Private.
[02:34] Jordan Kim: We have SOC2 and ISO docs, and can provide HSM integration notes; we'll attach those to the postmortem.
[02:41] Priya Menon: Ok. Let's be explicit on timelines. Short-term we want something in prod within 2 weeks — cache tuning + canary autoscaler policy. Medium term evaluate Dedicated pool for Black Friday next year.
[02:55] Mikhail Petrov: Actionable plan: 1) immediate KV TTL changes and reduced cache eviction thresholds; 2) a canary rollout of the autoscaler policy with a rollback hook; 3) add extra telemetry to capture per-request prefix hit rates for 48 hours after change. We'll need request traces from Atlas for the S2 window to reproduce.
[03:17] Tom Alvarez: We'll pull the traceIDs and payloads and upload them to the share. Expect that today.
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: Great. A few clarifications — when you say "cache TTL changes" are you modifying client-side TTLs or server-side?
[03:34] Ravi Desai: Server-side. Our current client TTL is low because of a previous bug, which increased miss traffic.
[03:40] Mikhail Petrov: That matches — server-side TTL bump is recommended but with a staged increase. We don't want to keep stale prefixes too long.
[03:47] Priya Menon: There's also the question of cost. If we pre-warm and reduce eviction, token cost could go up; we need to balance cost v latency.
[03:56] Lena Ortiz: Right — that's the latency vs cost tradeoff. Redwood Optimize can run a quick sim with your request mix to estimate token/unit cost delta. I'll arrange that.
[04:06] Priya Menon: Is that a paid feature?
[04:09] Lena Ortiz: We can do an initial small sim free as part of the incident follow-up. Any deeper consult might be billable.
[04:15] Samantha Lee: About Dedicated — what is the expected lead time if we want a dedicated pool? Procurement and infra need numbers.
[04:23] Lena Ortiz: Typical lead time for Dedicated in our current regions is 4-6 weeks for provisioning and agreement, longer if you need on-prem or VPC Private deployment. I'll send the procurement packet.
[04:33] Ben Carter: Regarding Private deployment — we need to understand the audit surface: where logs live, encryption at rest, ability to use our KMS. Also does Redwood support bring-your-own-HSM?
[04:44] Jordan Kim: BYO-HSM is supported in Private deployments; for Hosted we offer KMS integration managed by Redwood with explicit audit logs. We'll attach the doc with the differences.
[04:55] Tom Alvarez: Back to the incident — there was also a spike in error rates tied to a particular prompt template. Could prompt tokens have driven longer sequences and triggered kernel path differences?
[05:07] Mikhail Petrov: Yes, long-tail sequences change memory use and can hit different execution kernels which sometimes are slower. We did see a shift in sequence length distribution in that window.
[05:18] Priya Menon: So we should also look at prompt shaping as a mitigation? Shorten system prompts or chunk?
[05:24] Mikhail Petrov: Exactly — prompt shaping + early exit heuristics can reduce avg token generation and latency. We'll give examples.
[05:32] Ravi Desai: Is there an easy way to get per-route token breakdown in the console? Our telemetry is currently coarse.
[05:40] Jordan Kim: We can enable token-level breakdowns for a short retention window for debug purposes. There will be a small additional cost to retain high-granularity telemetry.
[05:52] Priya Menon: Ok, then step one: we want Redwood to share the condensed postmortem and the recommended kv/ autoscaler config. Step two: we'll run those changes in staging and attempt to reproduce. Step three: schedule the canary.
[06:06] Lena Ortiz: Confirmed. Also pro tip — set a fallback route to a <=1.5x latency model variant during peaks instead of regional failover; that often keeps throughput without cross-region latency penalty.
[06:18] Tom Alvarez: That makes sense. Any risk of semantic degradation to that approach?
[06:22] Mikhail Petrov: Slight model quality drop on corner cases but typically acceptable for non-critical paths like autocomplete. For checkout specific flows we'll define acceptance thresholds.
[06:31] Priya Menon: How will we validate no data leakage when we pre-warm caches? We send PII sometimes.
[06:39] Ben Carter: We need explicit encryption in transit and at rest, and the pre-warm mechanism must not write ephemeral user context to any shared cache.
[06:46] Lena Ortiz: For Hosted we ensure cache keys are namespaced to customer and we do not share KV entries across tenants. We'll include a technical note describing key namespace scheme.
[06:56] Samantha Lee: Any quick wins to reduce tail latency now?
[07:00] Mikhail Petrov: Increase worker concurrency for low-latency routes, reduce batching window during peak windows, and enable prioritized micro-batching for checkout routes.
[07:10] Tom Alvarez: Will that increase token costs?
[07:13] Mikhail Petrov: Slightly — more concurrency can mean more small batches and higher per-token overhead. We can model it.
[07:20] Priya Menon: OK, let's talk rollbacks — if a canary goes bad, what's the fastest rollback?
[07:26] Lena Ortiz: We have API flags to revert routing and autoscaler changes instantly; those are part of the runbook. Additionally, we'll provide a 'kill-switch' playbook for Atlas.
[07:35] Ravi Desai: Who owns the runbook edits? Redwood or Atlas?
[07:38] Jordan Kim: We'll prepare the first draft. Atlas will review and then it becomes the joint runbook.
[07:44] Priya Menon: We need better alerting thresholds — yesterday some of our SRE pager rules didn't catch the degradation early.
[07:52] Tom Alvarez: We'll add per-route 99th latency thresholds and error-rate percentiles. Redwood, can you suggest an SLI/SLO set?
[07:59] Mikhail Petrov: Yes, recommended SLOs: 95p latency < 250ms for checkout autocomplete, 99p < 600ms, error rate < 0.5%. We'll formalize in the doc.
[08:12] Priya Menon: How about a performance regression test we can run before big events?
[08:18] Lena Ortiz: We can run a pre-event smoke test with synthetic load and a target 30-minute soak. Redwood Optimize can script this with your sample traffic.
[08:26] Samantha Lee: Cost aside, is Dedicated the only way to guarantee we don't see autoscaler oscillation in peak?
[08:33] Mikhail Petrov: Dedicated greatly reduces variability because you have capacity isolation, but autoscaler tuning and pre-warm strategies can mitigate a lot of cases on Hosted. Dedicated is the stronger guarantee.
[08:44] Priya Menon: Procurement will need numbers and contract language for Dedicated. Lena, you'll send that?
[08:49] Lena Ortiz: Yes I'll attach the Dedicated pricing and SLA excerpt.
[08:53] Ben Carter: One more security ask — we need longer retention for audit logs for 365 days for certain flows. Can Redwood support that?
[08:59] Jordan Kim: For Hosted we can extend retention as an add-on; for Private it's typically customer-managed. We'll include options and pricing.
[09:08] Tom Alvarez: Alright let's run through an explicit timeline.
[09:12] Priya Menon: Short term (0-2 weeks): KV TTL bump in staging, autoscaler canary plan, add token-level telemetry. Medium (2-6 weeks): Canary to small % in prod, post-cana ry analysis, procurement starts for Dedicated if cost analysis favors. Long (>6w): Dedicated provisioning or Private evaluation.
[09:34] Lena Ortiz: Noted. I'll create a JIRA for the runbook edits and the canary plan. I'll also share the condensed postmortem slides and perf snippets by Friday (2026-12-10).
[09:44] Mikhail Petrov: I'll put together the perf command-line steps, a short dockerized reproducer, and the autoscaler policy patch.
[09:52] Tom Alvarez: We'll upload the trace bundle today and kick off staging runs.
[09:56] Priya Menon: And I'll loop in procurement and security to the follow-up thread.
[10:01] Jordan Kim: Ben, any blockers from security to start rolling the staged TTL changes?
[10:06] Ben Carter: We'll need the namespace doc and the KMS integration notes first. If those look good we can approve a limited change.
[10:14] Lena Ortiz: We'll attach both and mark the change as limited scope.
[10:18] Priya Menon: OK final recap please — who owns what, and dates?
[10:23] Lena Ortiz: Recap: Redwood (Mikhail) — perf steps + autoscaler patch (due 12/10); Redwood (Lena) — procurement & postmortem slides + Dedicated pricing (due 12/11); Atlas (Tom) — traceIDs and sample payloads upload (due 12/09); Atlas (Ben) — security doc feedback (due 12/12). Next sync: after staging runs — propose 2026-12-15.
[10:44] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:48] Priya Menon: Thanks.
[10:50] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all. We'll follow up in the shared thread and I'll send calendar for the Dec 15th check-in.

End of transcript.
